items.front: First Governor-General of Bengal & the Act?
items.back: Warren Hastings, under the Regulating Act of 1773. Founded Asiatic Society of Bengal (1784).
items.examPoint: Warren Hastings — first Governor-General of Bengal & Regulating Act (1773)

items.back: Permanent Settlement (1793); 'Father of Civil Services in India'.
items.examPoint: Lord Cornwallis — Permanent Settlement & father of civil services in India

items.back: Permanent/Zamindari — Cornwallis (Bengal); Ryotwari — Read & Munro (Madras/Bombay); Mahalwari — Holt Mackenzie & R.M. Bird (NW Provinces).
items.examPoint: Land-revenue settlements — Permanent/Zamindari (Cornwallis), Ryotwari (Read & Munro), Mahalwari (Holt Mackenzie & R.M. Bird)

items.front: Wellesley — system & Fort William College purpose?
items.back: Subsidiary Alliance (1798); founded Fort William College (1800) to train British civil servants. It did NOT aim to give the Company a fixed income.
items.examPoint: Subsidiary Alliance features & Fort William College purpose; educational founders (Calcutta Madarsa–Hastings, Sanskrit College Benaras–Duncan)

items.back: Abolished Sati (1829); first Governor-General of India (Charter Act 1833); backed English Education Act (1835).
items.examPoint: Lord William Bentinck — abolition of Sati, English Education Act & first Governor-General of India

items.back: Doctrine of Lapse; first railway (Bombay-Thane 1853); telegraph; Wood's Dispatch (1854).
items.examPoint: Lord Dalhousie — Doctrine of Lapse, railways, telegraph & Wood's Dispatch

items.front: Who was last GG & first Viceroy?
items.back: Lord Canning; GoI Act 1858 abolished the EIC and transferred power to the Crown.
items.examPoint: Lord Canning — last Governor-General, first Viceroy & Revolt of 1857

items.front: Vernacular Press Act — imposed and repealed by?
items.back: Imposed by Lytton (1878); repealed by Ripon (1882). Ripon = 'Father of Local Self-Government' + Ilbert Bill.
items.examPoint: Lord Ripon — local self-government (Father of Local Self-Government) & Ilbert Bill

items.back: Removing the disqualification barring Indian magistrates/judges from trying Europeans (under Ripon).
items.examPoint: Lord Ripon — local self-government (Father of Local Self-Government) & Ilbert Bill

items.front: Partition of Bengal — made & annulled by?
items.back: Curzon partitioned Bengal (1905); annulled by George V at the 1911 Delhi Durbar (Hardinge II), capital shifted to Delhi.
items.examPoint: Lord Curzon — Partition of Bengal (1905), Indian Universities Act & archaeology (ASI)

items.back: Separate electorates for Muslims (Indian Councils Act 1909), under Lord Minto II. Muslim League founded 1906.
items.examPoint: Lord Minto II — Morley-Minto Reforms (1909) & separate electorates

items.back: Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms/dyarchy (1919), Rowlatt Act, Jallianwala Bagh (1919).
items.examPoint: Lord Chelmsford — Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms (1919), Rowlatt Act & Jallianwala Bagh

items.back: Civil Disobedience & Dandi March (1930), First RTC, Gandhi-Irwin Pact (1931).
items.examPoint: Lord Irwin — Civil Disobedience Movement, Dandi March & Gandhi-Irwin Pact

items.front: Last Viceroy & first GG of free India?
items.back: Lord Mountbatten (June 3rd Plan, 1947). C. Rajagopalachari succeeded him as first Indian GG.
items.examPoint: Lord Mountbatten — last Viceroy, June 3rd Plan & first Governor-General of free India

items.back: Relationship between the Crown/Government of India and the princely states (paramountcy).
items.examPoint: Committees — Butler Committee (1927, Crown–princely states), Hunter Commission & Wood's Dispatch
